samples.summary: The new label-removal branch reads `areas.ciConfig === false` as "this PR does not touch CI config", but the producer emits `ciConfig: false` for every *unknown* resolution too, so a fail-safe run silently clears a truthful `ci-config-changed` label
samples.evidence: Producer side, out of diff: `FULL(reason)` at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:470-477 returns `{ full: true, heavy: true, packages: [], tags: [], ciConfig: false, ... }` for every fail-safe route — "no diff base could be resolved" (line 546), "could not diff …" (line 550), "WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS was not valid JSON" (515) — and `classify` likewise returns `ciConfig: false` for the unmapped-path full run (line 430) and the empty-diff full run (line 455). Consumer side, new in this diff: `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:280` guards only on `areas` having parsed (`else if (areas)`), not on the resolution actually having been computed, and calls `removeLabel` at :284. So a PR that really did change `harness.config.json` but whose next run failed to resolve refs (shallow clone, missing head sha, unparsed hand-off) gets a `ciConfig: false` resolution and has its label removed, which is exactly the "stale label the reviewer cannot trust" the change set out to fix — only inverted. The comment at ci-report.yml:281-283 claims the branch fires only when the resolution is known; the producer contract does not support that. Fix belongs on the consumer (require e.g. `areas.full === false || areas.ciConfig === true`) or on the producer (distinguish unknown from false).

samples.summary: Marking packages/design-editor inert also removes it from the other `anyPkg` lane, `verify:doc-index`, which was not compensated with a `designEditor` tag the way `verify:entropy` was
samples.evidence: scripts/verify-self.mjs:194-199 declares `verify:doc-index` with `anyPkg: true, tags: ["docsProse"]`. Before this change a packages/design-editor edit landed in `resolved.packages` and selected it via `anyPkg`; now the inert match short-circuits the packages/ classification (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:406-411), so `packages` is empty and only `designEditor`-tagged lanes run. The diff reasons about exactly this hazard for `verify:entropy` (verify-self.mjs:361-370) but leaves doc-index unmentioned. Impact is small — scripts/verify-doc-index.mjs:231-236 checks package *directories* against packages/README.md and README.md, and a design-editor-only change rarely adds one — but the gate is now unreachable from that path, the same shape of gap the change is fixing.

samples.summary: The `verify-self` fail-safe comment in ci.yml still describes the pre-change mechanism ("the depth-1 checkout makes `git diff` fail"); with `resolveRefs` the run now bails one step earlier, at ref verification
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:183-187 documents the degradation path as: empty `WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS` → `resolve()` recomputes → depth-1 checkout makes `git diff` fail → full run. After this diff, `resolveRefs` (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:277-292) verifies `payload.pull_request.head.sha` with `rev-parse --verify` first; in the depth-1 checkout at ci.yml:210 that object is absent, so it returns `null` and `resolve()` short-circuits at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:546 ("no diff base could be resolved"). The outcome is still a safe full run, but the comment names a mechanism that no longer runs, and it is the comment a future reader will trust when changing checkout depth.

verdict.reason: Verified both halves in the repo. Producer: scripts/changed-areas.mjs:470-477 (`FULL`) emits `ciConfig: false` for every fail-safe resolution, including "could not read the CI mapping" (:542), "no diff base could be resolved" (:546), "could not diff ..." (:550), and the hand-off failures (:515, :525); `classify` likewise returns `ciConfig: false` for the unmapped-path full run (:430) and empty-diff full run (:455). So `ciConfig: false` means both "no gating file changed" and "unknown". Consumer, new in this change: .github/workflows/ci-report.yml:280 guards only on `areas` having parsed (`} else if (areas) {`) and calls `removeLabel` at :284-289, so a fail-safe resolution clears a truthful `ci-config-changed` label; the comment at :281-283 explicitly claims the opposite ("A missing resolution means we do not know what changed, and guessing 'not a config change' would quietly clear a label that is telling the truth"), which the producer contract does not support. Reachability confirmed: `resolve()` returns (never throws) on these routes, so .github/workflows/ci.yml:155-173 still writes/uploads areas.json with `ciConfig: false`, which ci-report.yml:157 reads — including for a PR that edits harness.config.json into invalid JSON (readCiConfig throws -> FULL at :542) or whose head sha cannot be verified (resolveRefs null at :285/:292). This is a consumer relying on a semantic the out-of-diff producer contract does not provide — in-lane for blast radius, not statable from the diff alone.
